o1.biggest_strength: Rigorous worked numbers that discount fit-finder users' self-selection (9.5 points, not 19) and a 50/50 portal test with a 10% holdout and a guardrail on time to refund.
o1.biggest_mistake: It has no day-3 'still on track' update, which is the cheap fix aimed at the day 3-5 ticket spike. It gives a single point estimate for each lever, and the post-delivery fit email is generic rather than a real fit guide for first-time bra buyers.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add a day-3 reassurance message and real bra fit guidance after delivery, show low and high ranges instead of single targets, and trim it to the 1,000-word limit.

o2.biggest_strength: It includes a day-3 'nearly there' update and a delivered email that coaches bra fit in plain words ('comfort beats the number on the tag'). Its numbers are low-to-high ranges whose working checks out.
o2.biggest_mistake: The portal pre-selects Swap for size reasons, which is a gentle nudge that could feel like pressure, and it never says how the portal change will be tested. It also invents a 2-hour order-edit window and makes a free-switch promise from it.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Make the swap first but not pre-selected, add a portal A/B test with a guardrail metric, and confirm the order-edit window rather than assuming it.

reason: I'd rather have Output 2: it covers all three fixes in our voice, adds the day-3 update, gives first-time bra buyers real fit help after delivery, and gives honest ranges. Output 1 has tighter test design, but it misses the day-3 message and uses single point targets.
